title.value: Group Robust Classification Without Any Group Information
title.justification: The title accurately reflects the content of the paper, which discusses classification methodologies that do not require any group information, particularly in the context of addressing biases.

extractions.description: This paper addresses the limitations of empirical risk minimization (ERM) due to its susceptibility to spurious correlations and the need for costly bias annotations to estimate group-balanced or worst-group accuracy. It proposes a revised methodology for training and validating debiased models in an entirely bias-unsupervised manner, utilizing pretrained self-supervised models to extract bias information. The proposed approach demonstrates robust accuracy improvements in synthetic and real-world tasks, outperforming state-of-the-art methods that rely on bias labels.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily addresses methodological improvements in group robust classification, which is not directly related to eco-responsible AI categories such as climate change or pollution.

primary_sub_category.justification: The main focus of the paper does not align with any specific eco-responsible sub-category. It is centered on improving group robustness in machine learning models.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on developing methodologies to enhance classification models' robustness to biases without relying on explicit group labels, a topic that could be classified as a new category in machine learning.
new_primary_category.quote: To address these limitations, we propose a revised methodology for training and validating debiased models in an entirely bias-unsupervised manner.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-category is suggested to capture the unique focus of the paper on achieving group robustness in classification without the need for any group information, which is a central theme of the research.
